overview: Fungal infections span a huge range of severity, from a cosmetic nuisance on skin to a life-threatening disseminated illness.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Fungal infections confined to the outermost layers of skin, hair, or nails, with no tissue invasion.
aspects.valueB: Fungal infections that spread through the bloodstream to internal organs, often originating from lung inhalation.

aspects.label: Tissue Depth Involved
aspects.valueA: Limited to keratinized, non-living tissue (stratum corneum, hair shaft, nail plate).
aspects.valueB: Involves deep organs — lungs, liver, spleen, central nervous system, bone.

aspects.label: Typical Host Immune Status
aspects.valueA: Occurs in immunocompetent individuals as a common, usually benign condition.
aspects.valueB: Often occurs in, or is far more severe in, immunocompromised hosts, though endemic mycoses can affect healthy people too.

aspects.label: Examples
aspects.valueB: Histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, invasive aspergillosis, cryptococcal meningitis.

aspects.label: Severity / Mortality Risk
aspects.valueA: Rarely life-threatening; primarily a cosmetic or mildly symptomatic concern.
aspects.valueB: Can be life-threatening, especially without prompt antifungal therapy.

aspects.label: Treatment Approach
aspects.valueB: Requires systemic antifungal therapy (e.g. amphotericin B, azoles), often for prolonged courses.
